clue.text: Endless beer? Get round with soft drink

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
to cop is slang for to get or catch
O is round in shape
p (piano) means soft in music

explanation.surface: A drinker whose beer never runs out is told to buy a round of soft drinks instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft drink' looks like the definition, but 'soft' is the musical P and the definition is just 'drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet, bottled alcoholic beverage, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Medicine can start to taste awful, stopping relief

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so these letters fill the middle of the next word

parts.note: aid is relief or help

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so these letters are messed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of taste

explanation.surface: A medicine whose foul taste gets in the way of the relief it brings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like the verb 'is able to', but it is just letters to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: An antacid is a remedy that neutralises stomach acid, a common over-the-counter drug.

clue.text: One in caravan approached lake

parts.note: came is the past tense of come, to approach
L is short for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Someone towing a caravan drives up to a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caravan' suggests a holiday trailer, but here it is a desert procession of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Camels are the pack animals that make up a desert caravan, so one is a member of it.

clue.text: Dish that's oddly priced

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered positions, the first, third and fifth

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of priced

explanation.surface: A menu dish with a strange price tag.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a baked dish of pastry with a filling, a common meal.

clue.text: Pressure to design and match outfit

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
to lay plans is to devise or design them
to suit is to match, as colours suit each other

explanation.surface: A designer under pressure to create a coordinated outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A playsuit is a one-piece garment of top and shorts, a type of clothing outfit.

clue.text: Leader finished with band that's very entertaining

indicators.note: to entertain is to host guests, so this word holds the others inside it

parts.note: so can mean very, as in 'so good'
time is up when it is finished
R.E.M. was an American rock band

explanation.surface: A boss who has just finished work joins a band that is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very' gives two letters that split to wrap around the rest, a common container trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge of an organisation or activity, its head.

clue.text: Scales to go up: Yankee is heavy

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading from bottom to top, the other way round

parts.note: to scale fruit or fish is to peel off its skin
Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Bathroom scales go up: an American finds they are overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scales' looks like a weighing device but is a verb meaning removes the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy can describe eyes or a person drowsy and ready for sleep, as in heavy-lidded.

clue.text: Fishing line in stormy Eastern port

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Anglers fishing in a harbour on a rough day out east.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the Lord's Prayer, a paternoster is a weighted angling rig with hooks spaced along it.

clue.text: Pleasing noises from Brussels; they're not genuine

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union
phonies are fakes, things not genuine

explanation.surface: Nice-sounding announcements from EU officials that are really fake.
explanation.walkthrough: Brussels is used as shorthand for the European Union's institutions.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphony is a pleasant harmony of sounds, so euphonies are agreeable sounds.

clue.text: Face deliveries by amateur

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries
lay means non-professional, as in a layman

explanation.surface: Facing balls bowled by an amateur cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' suggests a batsman facing the bowling, but it is a verb meaning to cover a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To face a wall or board is to coat its surface with another material, which is to overlay it.

clue.text: Make-up to entice, grabbing fellows on date

indicators.note: to grab something is to hold it, so this word takes others inside it

parts.note: to tempt is to entice
an era is a date or period in history
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Someone using make-up to lure blokes on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' looks like cosmetics but means a person's nature; 'on' in an across entry places one piece after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Your make-up is your character or nature, which is what temperament means.

clue.text: Writer's detailed writing

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, the word has its tail, its last letter, cut off

parts.note: a poem is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A writer known for richly detailed prose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'de-tailed': POEM loses its M to leave POE, Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was the American author of tales and poems such as The Raven.

clue.text: Some local vendor to deliver new stock

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the letters sit inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood seller asked to bring in fresh supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' looks like shop goods but means livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow that calves gives birth, delivering a new animal to the farmer's livestock.

clue.text: Another helping to wrap up old project

parts.note: an extra is one more, another

indicators.note: wrapping something up encloses it, so this word goes around the next

parts.note: a plate of food is a helping
O is short for old

explanation.surface: Seconds of food used to finish off an old school project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' is a verb here, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To extrapolate is to project known trends forward to estimate future values.

clue.text: A pitch with American running back on: for this?

definitions.text: A pitch with American running back on: for this?

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: US is short for American
per means 'a', as in five pounds per head
in cricket, to bowl is to pitch the ball

explanation.surface: An American running back on the field: the whole clue describes the big game itself.
explanation.walkthrough: A running back is an American football position, and the Super Bowl is that sport's championship, so the wordplay doubles as a description of the event.
explanation.definitionFit: The Super Bowl is the NFL's championship game, played on a pitch with running backs on it.

clue.text: Fit dog chasing bird

parts.note: a dove is a bird
to dog someone is to tail them

explanation.surface: A healthy dog running after a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like an adjective about the dog, but it is a verb; 'dog' is also a verb, to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To dovetail is to fit together neatly, like interlocking joints in woodwork.

clue.text: Clear signal to go after victory

indicators.note: after tells you which piece is placed second in the answer, behind the other

parts.note: V is the victory sign
a driver indicates to show which way they will go

explanation.surface: A clear signal to move on after a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' looks like an adjective but is a verb meaning acquit.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate someone is to clear them of blame or suspicion, proving them right.

clue.text: Convert fancy housing for dog, in retirement

indicators.note: to house something is to give it shelter inside

parts.note: 'My!' and 'Fancy!' are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: Fido is a stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: Turning a smart house into a retirement home for the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like an adjective for the house, but it is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To convert something is to change or alter it, which is what modify means.

clue.text: Bar hosting bash and bachelor party

indicators.note: a host has guests inside their home, so this word holds the others

parts.note: a cake of soap is a bar
to lam is to hit hard, to bash
B is short for bachelor, as in degree titles

explanation.surface: A pub hosting a celebration and a stag night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' and 'bash' both look like party words but are wordplay; a bar of soap is also called a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A clambake is an American beach gathering where seafood is cooked, a social party.

clue.text: Mostly inspect floor for ring

indicators.note: most but not all of the word is used, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to canvass is to examine or scrutinise

explanation.surface: Checking most of a floor while looking for a lost ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is a boxing ring; a floored boxer is 'on the canvas'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing ring's floor is covered with a stretched sheet of canvas.

clue.text: Company: was leader and main man moved on board?

parts.note: a theatre company is its cast
led means was in front, was leader

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe whose star actor has been transferred to the board.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a chessboard and the main man is the king; castling moves the king two squares beside a rook.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a player who has castled has moved their king and a rook in one special move.

clue.text: Draws on pad first draughts

indicators.note: first says the piece named just before it comes at the front of the answer

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home
to draw on resources is to use them

explanation.surface: An artist sketching on a notepad before a game of draughts.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts look like the board game but mean currents of air; a pad is slang for a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatus is gas in the gut; its plural names puffs of wind, as draughts are currents of air.

clue.text: Finance partners invested in needy, supporting son

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so this piece comes below the other

parts.note: S is short for son

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: the needy are poor
North and South are partners at bridge

explanation.surface: Business partners put money into a struggling firm to help a son.
explanation.walkthrough: Because this is a down entry, the supporting piece sits at the top only after the rest is stacked beneath it: son is read first.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance a project or event is to fund it, which is what a sponsor does.

clue.text: Performer in topless bar, model to pose bent over

indicators.note: without a top, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: bending something over turns it the other way, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: the Model T was an early Ford car
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: A performer in a topless bar told by the model to strike a bending pose.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T Ford is why 'model' can give a single T.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist can be any performer or entertainer, such as a singer or variety act.

clue.text: A record on air after release? Is group out of university playing hit

definitions.text: A record on air after release?

indicators.note: playing about with letters rearranges them
out of means without, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
U is short for university
to ram is to hit

explanation.surface: A record playing on the radio after its release, by a group from university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record on air' sounds like broadcasting but is a chart of breathing out after drawing breath in.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirogram is the tracing a spirometer makes of air breathed in and out, a record of exhalation.

clue.text: Playboy magazine's limits pushed in top cover without female

indicators.note: something pushed in goes inside the other word
without means lacking, so the abbreviation for female is dropped

parts.note: a roof is the cover on top of a building
F is short for female

indicators.note: limits are the edges, so only the first and last letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of magazine

explanation.surface: A Playboy magazine cover shoot with the woman removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playboy' looks like the magazine's name, but it is the definition, and 'magazine' is the next word's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romeo is a womaniser, after Shakespeare's lover, much as a playboy chases women.

clue.text: Earn millions before tax returns

parts.note: M is short for millions

indicators.note: something that returns comes back, so the letters run the opposite direction

parts.note: to tax someone is to tire them

explanation.surface: Earning millions before filing your tax returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax returns' looks like paperwork, but 'tax' is a verb meaning tire, which is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve it, much as you earn a reward.

clue.text: Field with good jumper, furlong to go

indicators.note: something still to go is to be removed, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a flea can leap many times its own length
F is short for furlong in horse racing

explanation.surface: A horse that jumps well in a field with a furlong left to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good jumper' suggests a showjumping horse, but it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a poetic word for a meadow or grassy field.

clue.text: Maidservant struggles and takes note

indicators.note: something struggling twists about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A housemaid having a hard time but paying attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To animadvert is to notice or comment on something, an old sense being to take notice.

clue.text: Fight scene's cut

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: a scene is a view, a landscape

explanation.surface: A fight scene edited out of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scene' and 'cut' suggest film editing, but scene is a landscape view, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to compete or contend with others, a mild form of fighting.

clue.text: Extremely low flower has greenfly?

parts.note: the Dee is a river, something that flows
greenfly is an example of a garden pest, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A low-growing plant infested with aphids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword pun: a thing that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepest is the superlative of deep, meaning lowest down, the furthest below.

clue.text: Flat season without maiden horse

parts.note: flat and even both mean level

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a term is a season or session, as at school
M is cricket shorthand for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A horse that won no maiden race during the Flat racing season.
explanation.walkthrough: The Flat is the British season of horse racing without jumps; here it just means level. A maiden is also a horse that has never won.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse trained for eventing, the equestrian competition combining dressage, cross-country and jumping.
